subject: doc:.claude/skills/mvp-mode/playbooks/autopilot-full.md
why: Owner answer 2026-11-24 on the Autopilot-stack proposal (option 1b, no stacking), with the coordinator's rulings on two critic rounds. steps diff: autopilot-full#1 traits +blocked-bead-waits. Intake lists every handed-over bead (an epic: its direct features) before filtering. A bead blocked by one still open, a feature of the same run included, waits while the run builds the others: under this workflow a feature delivered by pull request closes only once that merges, so the waiting one starts in a later run from a trunk that holds it. A code blocker (a feature, task or bug) closed with no merged pull request in its close reason (wontfix, a duplicate, by hand) proves nothing reached trunk, so the bead gets the human label and a comment naming the blocker and is held for the owner; a closed decision or closed human bead frees it, as Beads intends. Each bead is judged by two checks, never a guess: bd ready --limit 0 lists it (inherited blocks included; the default list stops at 100), and bd show on it and its ancestors finds the blocking edges, each closed code blocker then read by its own id (bd show <id> --json, its close_reason; a dependency line does not carry it); a feature's own child tasks keep step 3's ready-child order. When none can start, the run replies Not started before taking the run marker. The concurrency proposal's evidence is no blocking edge between the features proposed in parallel and files that do not overlap (P:90-117). Step 2 reruns step 1's whole blocker rule on the feature's current edges and close reasons just before its branch, worker and claim, with the same wait or hold (P:118-120). Step 6 opens the pull request with gh pr create --base <trunk> and reads its base back before any verdict, a base other than trunk stopping the feature (P:188-195). The reply requires every exit to list each bead not started at steps 1-2 and why: its blocker and that blocker's pull request if any, or else the actual reason (no acceptance, an open question, claimed by another actor, deferred); a waiting or held bead makes the run Partly finished once a feature started, and Not started when none did (P:241-243, P:249-254, P:258-260).

subject: cursor_plugins:playbook:pstack/skills/poteto-mode/playbooks/autopilot-stack
why: Map 2.19 (remedy: a branch of Autopilot-full, not a playbook that overrides it) and the owner answer of 2026-11-24 on the adaptation proposal (option 1b, no stacking). Upstream is Autopilot-full with two overrides. Override 1, stop at verified and never merge, is already Autopilot-full's: it never merges and ends each feature at a merge-ready pull request, merging held for the owner and left to Shipping (P:2, P:57-58, P:71-77, P:210-214). Override 2, stacking, is rejected: a Beads blocking edge holds a dependent until its blocker closes, and under this workflow a blocker delivered by pull request closes only after that pull request merges (Beads itself checks only closure), so stacking would add parent merges, a re-check after each and retargeting only to start the child earlier; and a run never force-pushes (P:78-80), which rules out rebasing a pushed child onto its parent. In its place Autopilot-full gains the blocked-bead rule: dependents wait, a code blocker closed without a merged pull request holds its dependent for the owner while a closed decision or closed human bead frees it, and the whole rule is rerun just before each feature starts (P:90-120); every exit's reply lists each bead not started with why, its blocker and that blocker's pull request, or else the actual reason (P:241-243); and the pull request opens on trunk, its base read back before any verdict (P:188-195). Supersedes the defer 2026-11-20-deferred-playbooks:006.

modifications: Stop at verified, never merge (override 1): already Autopilot-full's own rule; each feature ends at a merge-ready pull request and merging is held for the owner, done by Shipping on the owner's word (P:2, P:57-58, P:71-77, P:210-214). Nothing added for it.
The reply lists each pull request with its verdict instead of what merged: already Autopilot-full's reply (P:246-248).

A dependent feature waits instead of stacking: intake lists every handed-over bead first; one blocked by a still-open bead, one of the same run included, is not started and the run builds the rest; it starts in a later run from a trunk that holds its blocker. A code blocker (a feature, task or bug) closed without a merged pull request in its close reason (wontfix, a duplicate, by hand) holds the dependent for the owner with the human label and a comment; a closed decision or closed human bead frees it, as Beads intends. Judged per bead by two checks, bd ready --limit 0 listing it (inherited blocks included) and bd show on it and its ancestors finding the blocking edges, each closed code blocker then read by its own id (bd show <id> --json, its close_reason), and the whole rule rerun just before each feature's branch, worker and claim; a feature's own child tasks keep step 3's order (P:90-120).

Every exit's reply lists each bead not started at steps 1-2 and why, one requirement above the exit variants: its blocker and that blocker's pull request if any, or else the actual reason (no acceptance, an open question, claimed by another actor, deferred); Partly finished once a feature started, Not started when none did, and when nothing can start at intake the run replies before taking its marker (P:241-260, P:90-117).
Each feature's pull request targets trunk: opened with --base <trunk>, its base read back before any verdict, a different base stopping the feature (P:188-195); stacking's other base is never set.
deliberately_dropped: Stacking (override 2): a dependent pull request based on its parent's branch, rebased onto it, restacked when the parent gets a new head, with a verdict kept across a restack by patch-id. Beads blocking edges hold the dependent until its blocker closes; a blocker delivered by pull request closes only after that merge, and a closed decision or closed human bead frees its dependent without one, so stacking would add parent merges, a re-check after each and retargeting only to start earlier, and a run never force-pushes (P:78-80), which rules out rebasing a pushed child. Owner answer 2026-11-24. revisit_when: the owner wants dependent features built before their blockers merge.
A separate playbook and a stacks reference: the router has a called playbook run whole, so an override playbook cannot reshape Autopilot-full's steps; the one rule lives in Autopilot-full.
Naming the playbook in every loop tick's prompt: a run here is one session following one playbook, with no timed ticks.
